actual_prompt:
EDIT THE FIRST IMAGE ONLY. Retain its exact viewpoint, image framing and all architectural edges. The other images are material/detail samples, NEVER replacement room compositions. Do not recreate their camera. 

Create one photorealistic adaptation of Páfrány · Tölgy és smaragdzöld for apartment A902, camera Cam_03.

INPUT ROLES. Image 1: the exact apartment camera/geometry control. Images 2 onward: original Páfrány appearance references PF01, PF02, in that order. Match their actual colour, finish and furniture character closely while retaining the apartment layout. The proposed room pairing is a new design decision, not a claim about original project apartment numbers.

CAMERA. Use fixed Cam_03 K1, level and looking south from the northeast side, 20 mm at 1.50 m with the locked downward shift. The kitchen is the subject: show the two working runs, their front grid, worktops and splashbacks, the D13 refrigerator tower and the southern tall-unit wall. Dining and its ML04 pendant enter the right foreground. The TV wall and terrace remain outside the frame; the composition is an exact galley study rather than a second living-room hero.

APARTMENT-SPECIFIC LOCK. Keep the established 2.90 m principal shell and lower local ceiling returns. The approved TV wall and seating location face one another; maintain the established 3.00 x 2.40 m U-layout study without changing its footprint. Keep actual kitchen runs and dining position. Never change the terrace levels, steps or panorama.

PALETTE. Pale natural oak with closely spaced vertical flutes, soft concrete-grey woven fabric, forest-green velvet, muted bronze, white stone appearance with grey veins. Match the colour balance and grain scale in PF01–04.

ROOM DESIGN. Reproduce the PF01–02 grey finely woven sofa, simple slim arms and emerald accent cushions within the existing seating footprint. Give the existing full-height storage pale vertical oak fluted fronts and one narrow, useful bronze-backed illuminated display niche with glassware, not a new bar occupying circulation. The TV field is the quiet grey field paired with oak storage: this TV adaptation is designed for the apartment because the reference does not show a complete TV wall. Use a small round pale-stone coffee table, slim bronze base, grey upholstered dining chairs and restrained black continuous-line art on the existing art wall. Bring in the reference green velvet as a chair only if the control already has a chair position; otherwise express it on cushions. Keep the sofa light grey, not green. Finish with tailored light-grey curtains, white translucent sheers and a textured grey rug.

Transfer PF02 pale oak tall fronts, quiet matte-grey upper and lower units, white-and-grey veined worktop and splashback to the actual apartment kitchen. Preserve appliance, sink and hob positions and every existing working run. Place grey upholstered chairs around the approved table; give the table the quiet grey top and restrained bronze detail of the reference. A slender horizontal glass-and-bronze pendant may occupy the existing dining supply only. No reference island, new stool row or curved floor replacement.

ARCHITECTURE AND CAMERA LOCK. Image 1 is the existing furnished apartment view and is the exact camera, crop, room-shell and furniture-placement authority, not a source of the new style. Change the furniture finishes, detailing and permitted decorative panel faces to match the subsequent Páfrány reference images. Keep walls, ceiling outline, doors, windows, frames, service lids, radiator positions, floor material and plank direction unchanged. No borrowed garden, staircase, fireplace, island, double-height volume or ceiling system from the reference. Keep the true Budapest panorama and terrace steps/levels/railings. The prior images are unvalidated concepts: preserve their camera consistently but do not claim construction approval.

COMPLETE FURNISHING AND CONTINUITY. Render a complete lived-in but carefully styled room, including tailored floor-length opaque curtains with translucent sheers at real curtain positions, rugs, restrained cushions, practical full-height closed storage and precise furniture end panels. Preserve every cabinet footprint and appliance sequence; visible open shelving occupies only the existing joinery depth. One or two distinctive small objects are enough. Reverse views retain exactly the same colour map, grain direction, furniture and art. Show only objects physically in the camera frustum; do not rotate a bed or bring the headboard into a reverse view. Full-height cupboards meet the real local ceiling with a small installation tolerance.

LIGHT IS LUXURY. Use elegant physically shielded continuous warm-white furniture lighting, dimmable and Philips Hue-compatible, normally 2200–2700 K, with 2700 K in the evening scene. Fit strips inside aluminium and opal profiles without visible dots. Light the TV base underside and selected furniture-top edges, useful shelves, headboard backs, wardrobe interiors, kitchen work surface, bathroom mirror and vanity underside where visible and electrically feasible. Keep master-bedroom approximately three-metre concealed headboard-light intent and Hue Go pair at the bedside; functional wardrobe lighting may use a suitable independent system. Preserve the existing ceiling heating/cooling and actual electrical outlets. No new ceiling cove, false ceiling, new spotlight track, invented socket or assumed supply. A decorative ceiling fixture may replace only the existing fixture at the same point. Furniture driver access and all bathroom-zone electrical suitability remain to be verified. Do not show physically impossible glowing stone.

BATHROOM LOCK. In a view containing the washbasin, provide a useful floating vanity spanning from the dry side of the shower-glass boundary to the adjacent wall where that span exists. The basin is integrated or undermounted into the top, never a vessel sitting above it. Provide a fixed one-metre-long clear screen at the existing open shower edge; preserve the entry gap and actual shower footprint. Add accessible wall storage on the existing dry wall, using a surface-mounted cabinet rather than cutting an unverified recess. A shower-only reverse view must not gain a vanity inside its wet zone; the real vanity stays out of frame. Keep all sanitary positions and existing tiles. Provide a soft mirror halo, usable face illumination and restrained under-vanity glow from suitable actual connections.

PHOTOGRAPHY AND LIMITS. One landscape architectural photograph in the same aspect ratio as Image 1, straight verticals, realistic textile and mineral microtexture, controlled highlights, no orange wash, no text, people, watermark or collage. Show a bright, readable interior with warm layered lights still apparent. Material names describe visual appearances, not verified manufacturers or product codes. Exact SKU, finish composition, dimensions and cost require checking. No unannounced structural renovation or floor replacement. Keep the target budget: A811 and A812 each HUF 9 million plus HUF 1 million untouched reserve; A902 HUF 18 million plus HUF 2 million reserve. Bespoke bronze/glass/stone and feature fixtures are cost-risk items, not verified affordable products. This is a reference-led concept for subsequent geometry, electrical and procurement validation.

CONTINUITY INPUT. The last image is this exact new variant already generated in a different camera. Use its precise upholstery, cabinetry material map, artwork and lighting details for continuity, but never replace Image 1 camera with the last image.
